paper_title: MathOdyssey Benchmarking Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills in Large   Language Models Using Odyssey Math Data
caption: Mathematical problems across educational levels. We curate and categorize problems by difficulty and subject area.
model_annotation: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of mathematical problems across different subject areas and educational levels. The chart contains 13 slices, each representing a specific category such as “Algebra – Olympiad-level”, “Number Theory – Olympiad-level”, “Geometry – Olympiad-level”, “Combinatorics – Olympiad-level”, “Algebra – High School”, “Geometry – High School”, “Pre-Calculus – High School”, “Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level”, “Calculus and Analysis – University-level”, “Differential Equations – University-level”, “Probability – University-level”, “Statistics – University-level” and one unlabeled slice. The slices are labeled with both the subject and level, and include percentage values along with a numerical count in parentheses. Specifically, the percentages represented are 21.19%, 1.03%, 6.46%, 9.56%, 17.83%, 3.62%, 14.21%, 6.46%, 6.20%, 3.62%, 5.43%, 4.39%, and an unlabeled slice with approximately 3.62%. Percentage labels are positioned inside each slice, and the slices generally appear to be ordered in descending proportion from largest to smallest, starting with “Algebra – Olympiad-level”. A legend is not present, but each slice is individually labeled with its corresponding category.
